title: How to Run Partnership Ads on Meta: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: Learn how to run partnership ads on Meta with our step-by-step guide. Get setup instructions, creator authorization tips, scaling strategies, and troubleshooting for better performance.
body_markdown:
## Diagnosing Underperformance at Every Funnel Stage


When a partnership ad loses efficiency, identify where the customer journey breaks before changing the campaign. Review three stages: the ad earns attention, the offer motivates action, and the website completes the purchase. Compare results with your campaign objective and a relevant baseline, such as other ads sent to the same audience and destination. This prevents a weak click-through rate from being treated as a checkout issue, or a landing-page problem from prompting unnecessary creative changes.


### Is It the Creative? Diagnosing Hook, Retention, and Click-Through Issues


Start with delivery and attention signals. If impressions are coming in but people leave early, review the opening seconds, message clarity, and whether the product appears promptly. If viewers stay but few click, check whether the video explains the product benefit and gives a clear reason to visit the destination. Compare the ad’s hook, pacing, demonstration, captions, and call to action with stronger creative in the same campaign. Change one major creative element at a time so the next review can show what affected the result.


### Is It the Offer? When Price, Promotion, or Positioning Is the Problem


When clicks arrive but purchases do not, assess the offer before replacing the creator’s video. Confirm that the advertised price, promotion, product availability, shipping terms, and value proposition match what shoppers see after clicking. Ask whether the benefit justifies the price and whether the product page fulfills the ad’s promise. If the destination works and the message is consistent, test a more relevant promotion or sharpen the product positioning, then compare purchase behavior.


### Is It the Funnel? Landing Page and Checkout Red Flags


Check the full path on a mobile device, from ad click through checkout. Look for slow loading, broken links, mismatched product variants, unavailable inventory, confusing shipping costs, or checkout errors. Review landing-page views alongside purchases: a gap between clicks and page views can point to a loading or destination issue, while completed visits without checkout activity call for a closer review of the page, price, and purchase steps.


### Why Fixating on the Learning Phase Misleads Beginners


The learning phase describes delivery, not why shoppers fail to buy. Use it as context, then examine each funnel stage before making a change. Weak attention calls for a creative review; engaged viewers with few clicks may need a clearer message or call to action; clicks without purchases call for an offer and site review. Avoid making several edits at once, since that obscures which change influenced performance.


**Diagnostic rule:** Match the symptom to the stage. Repair the earliest clear break in the customer journey before adjusting later stages.
